body:
## Summary

Multipart upload is hard-refused with **501 NotImplemented** via the subresource denylist (`crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:170-207,269-275`). This is the biggest missing piece: S3's single `PutObject` ceiling is 5 GB, so **objects >5 GB are impossible**, and `aws s3 cp`/boto3 **auto-switch to multipart above ~8 MB** — so large uploads from default clients fail today.

## Scope for Alpha
Implement the full verb set and its state:
- `CreateMultipartUpload` (`POST /b/k?uploads`) → allocate an upload-id + session.
- `UploadPart` (`PUT /b/k?partNumber=N&uploadId=U`) → stage each part (RS-encode to chunks now; hold the part→chunk mapping under the session).
- `CompleteMultipartUpload` (`POST /b/k?uploadId=U`) → assemble the ordered parts into the object's chunk map in one metadata commit; return the S3 multipart ETag (`md5-of-part-md5s "-N"`).
- `AbortMultipartUpload`, `ListParts`, `ListMultipartUploads`.
- Remove `uploads`/`uploadId`/`partNumber` from the denylist and add routing.
- **Design decision:** where the multipart **session + staged-part** state lives (metadata keyspace vs a dedicated store) and how orphaned/aborted parts are GC'd (custodian).

## Acceptance
- `aws s3 cp <8+GB file> s3://b/k` (auto-multipart) round-trips byte-identical (`sha256` match).
- Aborted/abandoned uploads leave no permanently-orphaned fragments.

Depends on: object-metadata/ETag (multipart ETag). Interacts with #491 (denylist bypass — the new routing must not be evadable). Part of the 0.1-Alpha S3 completion epic.

title: s3: implement multipart upload (Create/UploadPart/Complete/Abort/List) — >5GB + default large uploads
